cohort: The study included 20 patients aged 20-42 years with complex atypical endometrial hyperplasia and low-grade stage 1 endometrial cancer, who wished to preserve fertility and were treated at the Royal Hospital.
finding: Fertility-sparing treatment for atypical endometrial hyperplasia and low-grade stage 1 endometrial cancer in reproductive-age women is feasible, however, obese patients (BMI >= 30) had a higher recurrence rate.
